method_transition.summary: • We introduce the Context-invariant Boundary Discrimination (CBD) loss, a boundary-focused contrastive objective that learns representations invariant to contextual shifts, significantly enhancing localization precision.

Second, we introduce the Context-invariant Boundary Discrimination (CBD) loss, a contrastive loss that enforces semantic consistency at challenging temporal boundaries, making their representations robust to contextual shifts and hard negatives.

problem_units.macro_problem_name: Augmentation Reliability and Distribution Shift and Invalid Query and Open-Set Temporal Retrieval
problem_units.micro_problem_name: Query-agnostic content mixing creates semantically false negatives
problem_units.micro_problem_question: How can context diversification avoid replacing backgrounds with clips that remain relevant to the query?
problem_units.failure_mode: Semantically related replacement clips are treated as negatives and provide contradictory supervision.
problem_units.root_cause: The augmentation samples replacement clips without measuring video-text relevance.
problem_units.why_existing_methods_fail: Background replacement breaks spurious correlations but ignores whether the inserted content matches the query.
problem_units.affected_scenario: Content mixing inserts a clip from another video that is nevertheless semantically related to the current query.

evidence.quote: It builds a video-text similarity-based pool of replacement clips to simulate diverse contexts while preventing the false negative caused by query-agnostic mixing.

problem_units.macro_problem_name: Temporal Context Robustness and Representation Granularity and Semantic Structure
problem_units.micro_problem_name: Temporal boundary representations change under diversified surrounding context
problem_units.micro_problem_question: How can boundary features remain semantically stable when the surrounding temporal context changes?
problem_units.failure_mode: Boundary clips become hard negatives or shift representation when context is replaced.
problem_units.root_cause: Precise localization depends on local boundary evidence as well as surrounding temporal context.
problem_units.why_existing_methods_fail: Standard alignment objectives do not explicitly enforce context-invariant boundary consistency.

evidence.quote: Second, we introduce the Context-invariant Boundary Discrimination (CBD) loss, a contrastive loss that enforces semantic consistency at challenging temporal boundaries, making their representations robust to contextual shifts and hard negatives.
